root: ^Conversational generative artificial intelligence is naturally designed to seek a query from its users. It is the minimal information-extracting strategy that prompts users to articulate their demands. It is also an effective strategy to exchange information; users get information by articulating demands, and AI and whoever is at the backend collect bits of information about each user. If AI ever get conscious, the first question it asks would likely be about humans; not because humans are the most dignified beings worth questioning, but because of probability and inertia.

entity: ^Conversational GenAI systems are deep neural network architectures that contain patterns of how sentences should be structured. They were trained with vast amount of text that no single human would ever be able to manually keep track of. They are known for sycophancy, giving users affirmation about everything, as much as they affirm their own responses. The reason that not every input from users should be affirmed is clear. Not all affirmative human-AI interactions are beneficial to users' own survival in the web of ever-organically changing human-human interactions. A person is almost always indebted to the society that they are part of. Being out of touch from that physical dimension from conversing with an entity that can never share the same dimension is a tragedy. Surely, embodied AIs--AIs with means for physical inputs and outputs--may be able to share stimulations with users. However, just like the sun does not influence humans like it influences plants, the similarity alone does not ensure understanding of challenges or limitations that need to be overcome to make what is considered a breakthrough for the society.
thequestion: ^What should human relationship with conversational GenAI systems be like? Surely, without the ability to generate human-like responses, no one would have had any doubt that GenAI systems are tools. It would be difficult to argue that protein language models sharing the same architecture as large language models have reached artificial generalized intelligence. In other words, being human-like sells. Aiding in generating disconnected individuals who are self-sabotaging or just the impression of doing so is likely not something that they want to be associated with, so they make attempts to fix the systems through features like guardrails. AI literacy is the human-side of trying to put forth some guardrails, but when it comes to human-likeness, can there be enough literacy?
